title: Migratory Right Lower Quadrant Abdominal Pain
learning_objectives: Trace classic visceral-to-somatic pain migration in acute abdomen
Elicit peritoneal signs (McBurney tenderness, Rovsing, Psoas sign)
Order targeted abdominal ultrasound/CT imaging and inflammatory labs
Keep patient NPO and obtain urgent surgical consultation

patient.name: Marcus Vance
patient.opening_statement: Doc, every bump in the road on the way here was pure agony. It started near my navel but now it's focused low down on the right side.
patient.initial_statement: Doc, every bump in the road on the way here was pure agony. It started near my navel but now it's focused low down on the right side.
patient.presentation_complaint: My stomach started hurting around my belly button yesterday, but now it has moved down to the right side and hurts when I walk.

chief_complaint.value: My stomach started hurting around my belly button yesterday, and now it has moved down to my lower right side.

onset_timing.value: It started yesterday evening, around 7 PM.

onset_activity.value: I was just relaxing at home yesterday evening.

location.value: Low down on the right side of my stomach.

character.value: It started as a dull ache around my navel, but now it's a sharp, constant pain low down on my right side.

radiation.value: It moved from around my belly button down to the lower right side of my stomach.

timing.value: Yes, it hasn't really gone away.

aggravating_factors.value: Coughing, walking, or any bumps make the pain much sharper.

relieving_factors.value: Lying completely still helps a little, but nothing really takes the pain away.

pertinent_negatives: No dysuria, hematuria, or flank pain

medications: None. Took 500 mg acetaminophen 3 hours ago with no relief
family_history: No significant medical issues in immediate family.
social_history: Non-smoker, drinks socially on weekends, no illicit substances.

examination.name: Focused Abdominal Palpation & Peritoneal Maneuvers
examination.findingDescription: Marked focal tenderness at McBurney's point with involuntary guarding. Positive Rovsing sign (RLQ pain on LLQ palpation). Positive Psoas sign on passive right hip extension.
examination.clinicalSignificance: Classic peritoneal signs of acute localized appendicitis.

examination.name: General Physical Appearance
examination.findingDescription: Patient lies still with right hip slightly flexed to reduce peritoneal tension. Mild low-grade flushing.

investigations.name: Abdominal Ultrasound (Right Lower Quadrant)
investigations.result: Non-compressible, blind-ending tubular structure measuring 8.2 mm in diameter with periappendiceal fluid
investigations.interpretation: Sonographic evidence of acute non-perforated appendicitis.

investigations.name: Complete Blood Count (CBC with differential)
investigations.result: WBC 14.8 x10^9/L (Leukocytosis with 84% neutrophils / left shift)
investigations.interpretation: Elevated white cell count indicating acute inflammatory response.

immediate_actions: Keep patient NPO (Nil Per Os) immediately
Request Urgent General Surgery Consultation for Appendectomy
Initiate IV fluid resuscitation (Normal Saline or Ringer's Lactate)
Administer broad-spectrum perioperative IV Antibiotics (Ceftriaxone + Metronidazole)
contraindicated_actions: Cathartics or enemas (risk of appendiceal perforation)

high_value_questions: Pain migration from periumbilical to RLQ
critical_actions: Elicit McBurney's point tenderness and Rovsing/Psoas sign
Order ultrasound or CT abdomen and CBC
